name: Where to add new code
description: New API feature: types in lua/nit/api/types.lua, fetcher in lua/nit/api/feature.lua, state in lua/nit/state/data.lua, display in lua/nit/display/. Tests at tests/{layer}/feature_spec.lua. New component: implement in layer dir, wrap in init.lua as a delegating function (e.g., function M.start() require('nit.review').start() end — init.lua defines wrapper functions, not re-exports via M.fn = module.fn). New user command: add to subcommands table in lua/nit/commands.lua, implement logic in appropriate layer. Layer dirs: api/, state/, display/ (signs, highlights, manager, comment_popup, thread_panel), orchestration/ (versioning, snapshot, queue), ui/ (highlights.lua only). Never create barrel files — import modules directly via full path.

content: LuaCATS type annotations required on all public functions. Classes use Nit.Namespace.ClassName format (e.g., Nit.Api.PR, Nit.State.DataModule). All public functions annotated with ---@param and ---@return. Optional fields marked with ?: Nit.Api.PR?, string?. Check with make typecheck (lua-language-server). Configured in .luarc.json with runtime LuaJIT, library: vim runtime + luv, path strict mode enabled.

Naming: snake_case for all function and file names (e.g., get_pr, set_files, fetch_pr). Test files: *_spec.lua (e.g., tests/commands_spec.lua). Module pattern: local M = {} at top, public functions as M.fn(), private functions as local function _helper(), always return M. UPPER_CASE for module constants. All modules at nit.* namespace.

File structure: lua/nit/ for core code, tests/ mirrors source layout (tests/api/, tests/state/, tests/display/), plugin/nit.lua for bootstrap. Layer dirs: api/, state/, display/ (signs.lua, highlights.lua, manager.lua, comment_popup.lua, thread_panel.lua), orchestration/ (versioning.lua, snapshot.lua, queue.lua), ui/ (highlights.lua only — highlight group definitions). Each layer has init.lua as entry point. Stylua: column width 100, 2-space indent, single quotes. Run make format.

No barrel files: do not create files that only re-export other files. Barrel files add boilerplate and indirection without value. Each module should be imported directly from its source. Exceptions only with strong justification.

name: ast-grep rule authoring
description: sgconfig.yml at repo root, rules in rules/bug-prevention/ and rules/conventions/. Binary is ast-grep (not sg). Rules use YAML: id, language, severity, message, ignores, rule. No 'constraints' field in v0.41.0 — use regex inside has/not for string matching. 'has: pattern:' fails for field chains like vim.log.levels.X; use 'has: regex:' instead. File-level rules: 'kind: chunk'. Makefile target: ast-grep scan lua/ plugin/. GitHub Actions: ast-grep/action@v1.

ast-grep regex negation fails for multiline API calls: regex: 'nvim_set_hl\(\d+,' misses multiline form where args are on separate lines. Use \s* between \( and \d+ to match optional whitespace/newlines: 'nvim_set_hl\(\s*\d+,\s*['"]Nit'. Discovered when require-nit-highlight-prefix falsely flagged all multiline nvim_set_hl() calls.
resolution: Use \s* after ( to handle both inline and multiline call forms in ast-grep regex patterns.

title: Codify expertise as enforcement rules
rationale: Rules enforce automatically at lint time; docs require humans to remember and apply them. The layer boundary rules added in this session are an example — the architecture was already documented, but adding ast-grep rules makes violations impossible to miss.
